name_en: Otsuka ninjin — a meter-long, deep-red winter carrot from Yamanashi's soft volcanic soil
summary_ja: 市川三郷町大塚地区の深い火山灰土「のっぷい」で育つ、長さ1メートル近くに伸びる長根のにんじん。甘みと香りが強く、正月の煮物に欠かせない縁起物として土地で受け継がれてきたとされる。
summary_en: A long-rooted carrot grown in the deep, soft volcanic soil called noppui in the Otsuka district of Ichikawamisato, said to stretch close to a meter. Sweet and fragrant, it's treated as a lucky vegetable for New Year simmered dishes.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 山梨県

name_en: Nozawana — the tall leaf turnip of Nozawa Onsen that gave up its root for the cold
summary_ja: 野沢温泉村を中心に信州で栽培されるかぶの変種の菜。京都の天王寺かぶが高冷地で根を太らせず、葉と茎だけが1メートル近くまで伸びる姿になったと伝わる。霜に当たるほど甘く柔らかくなるという。
summary_en: A leafy member of the turnip family grown around Nozawa Onsen and across Nagano. A Kyoto turnip is said to have stopped swelling its root in the cold highlands and instead grown leaf and stem nearly a meter tall. Frost is said to make it sweeter and softer.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 長野県

name_en: Botan kosho — a thick-fleshed, peony-shaped hot pepper from the highlands of northern Nagano
summary_ja: 北信の高冷地で受け継がれる肉厚のとうがらし。「こしょう」は信州でとうがらしを指す呼び名で、牡丹の花のように肩にしわが寄った丸い形が名の由来と伝わる。ピーマンのような姿に反して辛みは強いという。
summary_en: A thick-fleshed chili pepper kept alive in the cool highlands of northern Nagano. Kosho is the local word for chili, and the name is said to come from the peony-like creases on its rounded shoulders. It looks like a bell pepper, but the heat is said to be real.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 長野県

name_en: Hida beni-kabu — a crimson-skinned, white-fleshed turnip from the Hida highlands
summary_ja: 高山市丹生川町が発祥とされる、皮が鮮やかな紅色で中は白い丸かぶ。飛騨の冬を彩る赤かぶ漬けの原料で、八賀かぶから紅色の株が選び抜かれたと伝わる。高冷地の寒暖差が色と甘みを育てるという。
summary_en: A round turnip with vivid crimson skin and white flesh, said to have originated in the Nyukawa district of Takayama. It's the raw material of Hida's winter red-turnip pickle, said to have been selected from a crimson sport of the older Yaga turnip. The highland temperature swings are said to build its color and sweetness.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 岐阜県

name_en: Moriguchi daikon — a thumb-thin radish over a meter long, grown in river sand for pickling in sake lees
summary_ja: 岐阜市の長良川沿いと愛知県扶桑町の木曽川沿いで育つ、長さ1メートルを超え太さは親指ほどしかない細長い大根。砂が深く積もった石のない土が根をまっすぐ伸ばし、ほぼ全量が酒粕に漬ける守口漬けの原料になるとされる。
summary_en: A radish grown along the Nagara River in Gifu and the Kiso River in Fuso, Aichi, that runs over a meter long yet stays no thicker than a thumb. Deep, stone-free river sand is said to let the root drive straight down, and almost the entire crop goes into moriguchi-zuke, the sake-lees pickle.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 岐阜県

name_en: Shizuoka mizu-wasabi — true wasabi raised in terraced beds of cold mountain spring water
summary_ja: 静岡市有東木や伊豆の山あいで、湧き水を引いた階段状の畑に育てる本わさび。肥料に頼らず一年を通して冷たい清水だけで育て、根茎をすりおろすと鼻に抜ける辛みのあとに甘みが残るとされる。慶長年間の有東木が発祥と伝わる。
summary_en: True wasabi grown in terraced beds fed by spring water in the mountains of Utogi, above Shizuoka city, and on the Izu peninsula. Raised year-round in cold, clear water with no fertilizer, its grated rhizome is said to leave a hint of sweetness after the heat clears the nose. Cultivation is said to have begun at Utogi in the early 1600s.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 静岡県

name_en: Orido-nasu — a round, near-black heirloom eggplant from the Miho peninsula, revived from stored seed
summary_ja: 静岡市清水区三保の折戸地区に伝わる在来のなす。丸い巾着型で皮は黒みがかった濃い紫、へたのとげが鋭く、肉質が締まって甘みが濃いとされる。一度は栽培が途絶え、保存されていた種から復活したと伝わる。
summary_en: An heirloom eggplant from the Orido district of Miho, in Shimizu, Shizuoka. Round and purse-shaped, with skin so dark a purple it looks black, sharp thorns on the calyx and dense flesh with a concentrated sweetness. Cultivation once died out and is said to have been revived from seed kept in storage.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 静岡県

name_en: Horyo daikon — a white-necked Owari radish with a horn-like curve that holds together in long simmering
summary_ja: あま市甚目寺の方領地区が発祥と伝わる尾張の在来大根。首まで白く、先が牛の角のように曲がり、肉質が緻密で煮崩れしにくく、煮物にすると甘みが出るとされる。江戸期から栽培され、練馬大根の元になったという説もある。
summary_en: An heirloom radish of Owari said to have originated in the Horyo district of Jimokuji, now Ama city. White to the neck, with a tip that curves like a cow's horn, it has dense flesh that holds together in simmering and turns sweet in the pot. Grown since the Edo period, it's sometimes said to be the ancestor of Tokyo's Nerima daikon.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 愛知県

name_en: Misono daikon — a dry-fleshed, white-necked radish from Ise, grown to be wind-dried and pickled as Ise takuan
summary_ja: 伊勢市御薗町で育てられる白首の在来大根。宮川沿いの砂質土で育ち、収穫後に竿に掛けて干してから糠と塩に漬ける伊勢たくあんの原料になるとされる。水分が少なく干し上がりが早く、歯切れのよい漬物になるという。
summary_en: A white-necked heirloom radish grown in the Misono district of Ise. Raised in sandy soil along the Miyagawa River, it's hung on poles to dry after harvest and then pickled in rice bran and salt as Ise takuan. Low in moisture, it dries quickly and is said to keep a clean snap in the pickle.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 三重県
